title: Central Asia’s Diplomatic Balancing Act on Display from Bishkek to New York
gist: Central Asian states displayed their multi-vector balancing act at both the SCO's 25th-anniversary summit in Bishkek (Aug 31-Sep 1) and the 81st UN General Assembly debate, managing ties with the US and China while preserving bonds with Russia. The SCO's Bishkek Declaration condemned military strikes on Iran and opposed 'unilateral coercive measures', giving Washington plenty to dislike.

insights.claim: As the world moves toward multipolarity, the five Central Asian states must manage relations with the United States and China while preserving deep historical, economic and political ties with Russia, a balancing act on display in their 81st UN General Assembly speeches.
insights.so_what: Central Asian governments are likely to hedge rather than align, keeping the region open to Western, Chinese and Russian investment and resource deals simultaneously.
insights.quote: the five Central Asian states find themselves in a tight spot
insights.speaker: Bimal Adhikari

insights.claim: Kyrgyzstan hosted the Shanghai Cooperation Organization's 25th-anniversary summit on August 31 and September 1; Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan are SCO members, while neutral Turkmenistan stays formally out but occasionally attends as a guest.
insights.so_what: SCO membership anchors four of five Central Asian states in a China-Russia-led forum, constraining how far they can tilt toward Washington.
insights.locator: Three weeks before the debate opened
insights.speaker: Bimal Adhikari

insights.claim: The SCO is widely seen as a vehicle for Beijing and Moscow to limit Washington's footprint in Eurasia.
insights.so_what: SCO statements are a barometer of China-Russia coordination against US influence in Eurasia.
insights.quote: The SCO is widely seen as a vehicle for Beijing and Moscow to limit Washington’s footprint in Eurasia
insights.locator: Three weeks before the debate opened
insights.speaker: Bimal Adhikari

insights.claim: The 2026 SCO Bishkek Declaration firmly condemned military strikes on Iran and opposed 'unilateral coercive measures', positions the United States would dislike.
insights.so_what: Central Asian states signing onto anti-sanctions and Iran-strike language complicates US efforts to court them, e.g. on critical minerals and transit.
insights.quote: from a firm condemnation of military strikes on Iran to opposition to “unilateral coercive measures.”
insights.locator: Three weeks before the debate opened
insights.speaker: Bimal Adhikari
